claim: Absorption is not transmission, and BTC survival is not ecosystem health.
Volatility contraction after a flush is not recovery confirmation when ETH, breadth and transmission remain weak.
Pullback warning should study the sequence ETF deterioration, fear persistence, price weakness, leverage flush, dominance persistence, failed transmission and compression, not depth alone.

Early Rotation Pre-Trigger thresholds were stablecoin alt inflow 3D above 3%, large-cap alt volume share 3D above 4%, ETH/BTC below 0.032 and BTC dominance above 56. It is an early-window signal, not a buy signal.
Fake Rotation Type 3 receives a hard penalty and bullish hints must be filtered more aggressively than fake starts are rewarded.
Alt-specific stablecoin velocity and reserve drawdown were defined as observation-only research, not core evidence.
ETF-era altseason capital lifecycle should be staged as WAIT, PREPARE, DEPLOY, PROTECT, then WAIT or post-rotation.
PREPARE requires improving conditions through time. Three days is insufficient, seven days is watch-worthy, 14 days meaningful and 30 days high-confidence.
Deployment order is large caps, mid caps, small caps and microcaps last, contingent on widening participation.
Protection should begin when internal transmission weakens before obvious price collapse, reducing microcaps first, then small caps, then mid caps.
Adaptive learning was framed around signal reliability, forecast attribution, confidence compression, outcome delay mapping and regime-dependent weighting, all shadow-only.
BTC range 62,303.96 to 67,203.74 and ETH range 1,677.17 to 1,843.46 were recorded for week 25. Stabilization was tentative and not recovery or rotation confirmation.

claim: Canonical and automation components require explicit self-healing and degraded-mode semantics rather than hard failure solely from unavailable external paths.
Unknown or unavailable values must remain unknown, with locked enums and no interpolation or AI guessing.
